findings: 85 of 88 items with Give Interactive haven’t been updated in 60+ days and 80 in 180+. A “vendor follow-up due” check would flag nearly all of them, so the report leans on release labels and closed ideas instead. The strongest next step is reconciling against Give Interactive’s own ticket export, since 86 of these items already carry a ticket ID.
87 open items sit under a parent that’s already Done, almost all on TT. Closing them would shrink the TT board by about 25% without losing any open work.
270 of 342 TT items are in To Do and 105 are unassigned. Unassigned only counts as a QA failure once work has started, which is true for just 2 items.
Due dates are a TT habit
TT has 87 items with a due date and DVR has 6; GE, HSER, and IL barely use them. The past-due check mostly speaks to TT.
Time in status isn’t available for GE

Jira only exposes when the status category last changed, and every Give Interactive-held GE status shares one category. Showing how long an item has sat in Signatry Approved would need each issue’s change history, which is possible but slower.
None of the 495 open items has a fix version, so fix versions can’t stand in for a delivery commitment. Give Interactive release labels are the only commitment signal, and only 6 items carry one.

4 assignees (Acosta Ramsey, Ambrose Talbot, Merritt Wakefield, and Stanhope G. Nadine) aren’t in the Slack directory but still hold 29 open items, and Jira still lists all of their accounts as active. That’s an offboarding gap as well as a QA one: worth confirming they’ve left and deactivating the Jira accounts. 19 of their items can simply be closed.
IL has 1 open item, 948 days old and unassigned. It may be worth retiring the board from the work group.
spec: A single report across every key in jira_workspaces.work, with a board filter that scopes the headline, chart counts, ledger, owner table, and sections. Per-board views belong in Jira. Every per-board view is precomputed in Python; the page only selects one.
Lanes by whose move it is

Work items need "who's holding this" before "how old is it". Without lanes, vendor-held GE items would read as our stalled work. The lane comes from a per-board vendor status map in config: a vendor status puts an item in the vendor lane, any To Do-category status is backlog, and everything else is our move.
Work moves slower, so the aging strip runs 0–30 through 366+ days. Dots keep their positions when a board filter is active; other boards' dots fade to 12% and leave the tab order.
TT Legacy, GE Dawn, DVR Midnight (Ice in dark mode), HSER Heartfelt, IL light grey. A board without its own pair uses board_default.

Checked parent over open child: child of a closed parent. Bulb with check: closed idea. Bolt: empty epic. Hourglass: stalled on us, the only risk-colored glyph, in Jubilee. Open padlock: blocker cleared. Person with plus: started, unassigned. Calendar with "!": past due. Box: vendor release passed. Tag: no vendor ticket ID. Octagon: blocked or on hold. Person with ×: not in directory. Person with arrow: outside Technology. Drawer: backlog rot.
Close the loop, vendor commitments at risk, reassign, blocked, stalled on us, backlog to groom, no issues found. The last two are collapsed until a filter is active.
Why vendor staleness isn't a check

80 of 88 vendor items exceeded 180 days on the 24 Oct 2026 data, so a follow-up-due check would flag nearly all of them. Release labels and closed ideas are the signal instead; reconciling against the vendor's own ticket export is the recommended future input.

Jira reported every assignee as active, including four people who had left, and Microsoft 365 people search isn't authorized on this tenant (missing People.Read). If that permission is granted, prefer it and keep Slack as the fallback. Lookups are cached in state/directory_cache.json.

Directory matching is by display name. Parent and idea checks ignore the child's own status; nearly all 87 parent-closed items were untouched backlog on the fixture. DVR and HSER have no vendor statuses mapped yet. A day count is clamped at zero when an item was updated after noon today.
